title: Maths reference: Angles and shapes
summary: The words and methods from Angles and shapes, each with an example and, where it helps, a picture of the board.
_about: Maths cards for maths/angles (see snippets/maths.json for the format).

items.label: transversal
items.hint: Parallel lines go the same way and never meet; arrows (>>) mark them. A transversal crosses both, making eight angles.

items.label: corresponding angles
items.hint: The same place at each crossing (an F shape). With parallel lines they are equal.
items.board:
widget: parallel
t: 60
pair: a, e
items.shows: a and e: the same place at each crossing, both 120°

items.label: alternate angles
items.hint: Between the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal (a Z shape). With parallel lines they are equal.
items.board:
widget: parallel
t: 60
pair: c, f
items.shows: c and f: between the lines, opposite sides, both 60°

items.label: co-interior angles
items.hint: Between the parallel lines, on the same side (a C shape). With parallel lines they add to $180^\circ$: they are not equal unless both are $90^\circ$.
items.board:
widget: parallel
t: 60
pair: c, e
items.shows: c and e: between the lines, same side, 60° + 120° = 180°

items.label: vertically opposite angles
items.hint: Opposite each other at one crossing: always equal, parallel lines or not. Not one of the parallel-line pairs.

items.label: give a reason
items.hint: For each angle you find, name the rule: corresponding or alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles add to $180^\circ$; angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$.

items.label: interior angle
items.hint: An angle inside a shape, at one of its corners.

items.label: polygon
items.hint: A closed shape with straight sides: triangle (3), quadrilateral (4), pentagon (5), hexagon (6), octagon (8).

items.label: regular polygon
items.hint: All sides and all angles are equal, so each angle is the angle sum shared equally: a regular hexagon has angles of $120^\circ$.

items.label: angle sum of a triangle
items.hint: True for every triangle, whatever its shape or size: tear off the corners and they fill a straight line.

items.label: angle sum of a polygon
items.hint: Split it into triangles from one corner: a shape with $n$ sides makes $n - 2$ triangles. A pentagon: $3 \times 180^\circ = 540^\circ$.
